# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and extract its working instructions into reusable canon packs plus the project's own local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/). Use when a project has no established working style yet, or it exhibits a facet no pack covers — during bootstrap of a fresh/empty repo, or on an uplevel request.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-branch-status: Assess one branch's landed status — merged, already-in-main, superseded, orphaned, or genuine unmerged work — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single branch is safe to delete, judging by content not the ref's name (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-branches task hands you branches to assess).
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).
- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single PR should stay open, judging by its commits and diff not its title (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-prs task hands you PRs to assess).
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.
- writing-claudinite-skills: Authoring or changing a skill in the Claudinite corpus — SKILL.md conventions, where a skill's checks and tests live, catalog and pack wiring. Use when creating or editing a pack's skills/<name>/ in the canon; a consumer project's own agent docs are authoring-agent-docs' turf.
- writing-migration-plans: Where a plan and a design live, and how to order a plan's phases so nothing stalls mid-run — the plan is a tracking issue (never a plan document in the repo), the design doc carries only the end state with rationale and alternatives; front-load the out-of-band setup, write ALL the code including the cleanup and take one approval for the stack, then chain every execution step to the verification of the one before it as a queued continuation, and keep the tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use BEFORE writing any DESIGN.md, migration plan, phased implementation plan, rollout or cutover plan — including the moment you are about to create a docs/<initiative>/ file — and when working through a plan's tracking issue.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.mjs or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one — Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. - simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

{"number":1317,"title":"Extract the task execution/scheduling surface into a claudinite-tasks pack","body":"Tracking issue for the split of `engine/scheduler/` (52% of core, 8,106 lines) out of the engine and into a canon pack, so the engine is pack distribution only. End state and rationale: `docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` **§18** (folded into the mechanism's own design doc — no standalone document).

## Agreed end state (summary — DESIGN.md §18 is authoritative)

- `packs/claudinite-tasks/` owns the whole task surface: queue, executor, signals, task contract, calendar/anchor math, dispatch, run-records, code-work, delivery helpers (`land-pr`, `deliver-generated`), GitHub REST helpers, the two workflow stubs, the operational `.md`s, and the `implement-request` built-in as an ordinary pack task.
- `packs/claudinite-tasks/shared-code/*` is the pack's published import surface — the one sanctioned cross-pack import in the corpus (barriers-enforced). Consumers: claudinite-dashboard (title grammar, outcome decode, anchor math) and every pack task that delivers (delivery + gh helpers).
- Queue meta-machinery relocates in: `task-janitor` (from basics), `usage-fold` (from claudinite-growth), the task-declaration checks (from claudinite-growth worldRules) — and the simulator + scenario suite (`docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/`), the mechanism's executable spec, into the pack's own `test/`.

# Task dispatch without slots — the work-item queue

The mechanism lives in [`engine/scheduler/queue/`](../../engine/scheduler/queue/),
behind `taskScheduler.dispatch`. A continuation of the owner's sketch (2026-08-12, reproduced in Appendix A), played against twenty timed
scenarios ([SCENARIOS.md](SCENARIOS.md)) and the field's prior art
([RESEARCH.md](RESEARCH.md)), with the owner's eight decisions of 2026-08-13
recorded in §15 and folded into the sections they changed. The phase plan
belongs to a tracking issue, not here. It supersedes
the slot machinery of
[per-project-scheduling DESIGN §3–§5](../per-project-scheduling/DESIGN.md) and
amends several of its §12 decisions (each amendment is named where it happens).
What it does **not** touch: the task folder anatomy (§1), the precondition
contract, code-work and its secrets model
([task-code-work DESIGN](../task-code-work/DESIGN.md)), the outcome ceiling, the
security posture (the issue is data; behavior comes from tracked files), and the
usage-metrics records.

The shape in one paragraph: **work items are issues, available for work; any
number of executors pull from them — and an issue exists only when there is
work.** The generator — one scheduler run on the repo's one cron — asks each
recurring task's precondition when its anchor comes and files its work item
only on a yes (#1115, decision §15.28); a no is a row on the repo's one
**schedule board** issue, and a read the scheduler cannot make fails open into
an item the executor decides. An executor — a GitHub Action by default, but
anything that can read issues — picks up the next ready item, claims it by
label, re-evaluates the precondition (a chained stage re-derives world state):
on a go it runs the work step and hands off to agentic work (a CCR session
invoked by API); on a no-go it **closes** the item with the reason. Follow-ups,
fan-outs, urgency, and one-off forcing are all just *creating or waking work
items*. There is no slot id, no exclusive claim, and no label-event re-arm;
the one watermark is the board's declined rows, and it fails toward asking
again, never toward skipping.

## 18. The pack boundary — the mechanism as `claudinite-tasks`

The whole mechanism this document describes is a canon pack, `packs/claudinite-tasks/`,
activated by declaration like any other; the engine is **pack distribution only**. The test from
`extending.md` still decides engine membership — would every pack's content stop working without
it? — and the queue no longer passes it: a repo that declares no tasks pack runs no scheduled
work, and that is a supported state, not a degraded one.

### What the engine keeps, what the pack owns

**The engine keeps** what every pack relies on to *exist* in a repo: pack discovery and loading,
the checks runner and hooks, the migration mechanism, settings/version/self-test, and the
distribution half of the wiring converge — settings hooks, the rules index, `.gitattributes`,
the badge row.

**`packs/claudinite-tasks/` owns** everything whose subject is task work: the queue (planner,
executor, continuation, drain, workflow-failure escalation, leases, readiness, janitor rules,
the work-item and dispatch vocabulary), the task contract, signals, calendar/anchor math, the
model map, run records, code-work, the delivery lane (`land-pr`, `deliver-generated`) with the
GitHub REST helpers and tracker it rides on, the two workflow stubs, the operational documents
(`executor.md`, `deliver-pr.md`, `queue/instructions.md`), and the scheduling half of the wiring
converge (workflow content, hashed cron, anchor hours, routine endpoints).

`implement-request` (§16) is an ordinary task of this pack rather than an engine built-in — the
`model_from_request` fence becomes "only this pack's task declares it". Item titles minted under
the legacy `engine/implement-request` id decode forever (the stored-data rename rule); new items
carry the pack's id.

Task discovery stays structural and pack-agnostic: this pack's scheduler scans every *declared*
pack's `tasks/<name>/` directories, exactly as §5 specifies. The `tasks/` contribution slot is
interpreted by this pack — the same composition seam as `barriers`' contributed rules:
declaration plus data, never a cross-pack import.

Queue meta-machinery lives here rather than where it historically landed: `task-janitor` (§11's
sweeps), `usage-fold` (folds this mechanism's own run records and outcome labels), and the
task-declaration checks (`task-declaration-shape`, `task-code-work-env`) are this pack's tasks
and checks. The simulator and its scenario suite — the mechanism's executable spec — live in the
pack's own `test/`.

### `shared-code/` — the published import surface

`packs/claudinite-tasks/shared-code/*` is the pack's deliberate export surface: the one place in
the corpus another pack's code may import from a pack it `requires`. Enforced as barriers
configuration — everything of this pack *outside* `shared-code/` stays off-limits to other
packs, and no other pack gains an equivalent surface by existing.

What it carries is what external consumers demonstrably need: the work-item/dispatch **title
grammar** (§3 — a work item is a GitHub issue and its title is its identity), the
**outcome/status decode** over item labels including every legacy spelling (§4), the **anchor
math** (`periodMs`, `mostRecentAnchor`, `nextAnchor`), the **delivery helpers**
(`deliverGenerated`, `landPr`) and **GitHub client/REST helpers** any pack's worker uses to land
output, and task-declaration validation, which other packs' tests exercise.

Consumers: `claudinite-dashboard` (renders the queue's state; stays its own pack and declares
`requires: ['claudinite-tasks']`), and any pack whose tasks deliver PRs or generated files.

### Updates live in claudinite-lifecycle

The versioned update flows (engine update, pack update, install) are the `update` task's own
machinery and live in `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/`. They still execute from the freshly fetched
canon tree, so the flow code a member runs is always current; the old `updates/*` module paths
remain as callable shims until no fielded vendored worker names them (the rule that already
governs `updates/*` exports).

A repo that declares `claudinite-lifecycle` but not `claudinite-tasks` has no queue, so its
update task never runs: **updates are opt-in via the tasks pack**. The recovery and manual lane
is a human session running the update or adopt-pack skills — a member with a state it likes
keeps it, like any package manager without forced auto-update.

### Workflows: written once, then static

The two member workflow files are static after adoption: secrets travel as one fixed
`CLAUDINITE_SECRETS: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}` line (§14.4), the per-repo cron minute and anchor
hours are written once at adoption, and `run:` lines name **mount pack paths**
(`.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/…`) behind which everything converges nightly — a
release never edits the YAML again.

Consequently **no update flow touches `.github/workflows/`**, and the `pending-workflows/`
withhold lane does not exist: a structural change to the YAML itself (permissions, an actions
version bump) is an explicit, human-merged fleet PR event, not a lane the machinery must carry.
Adoption of `claudinite-tasks` (the adopt-pack skill, or bootstrap when the pack is declared at
init) scaffolds the two files and the CCR routine endpoints; the routines' stored prompts point
at the pack's operational documents in the mount.

Members' `claudinite-ci.yml` is untouched by any of this: it is seeded once by bootstrap when no
existing workflow runs the world sweep, is member-owned from then on, and belongs to the checks
surface.

### Alternatives considered

- **Scheduler in the engine.** Scheduling was 52% of core; every consumer vendored machinery
  only scheduled repos use, engine releases implied workflow-path churn, and "core" stopped
  meaning distribution. Rejected — the size and the boundary rot are what this boundary fixes.
- **Fold the queue into claudinite-lifecycle.** Removes the updates↔queue seam entirely, but
  couples "being a member" with "running scheduled work" — a repo could not take the lifecycle
  without the queue, and the tasks surface stops being independent. Rejected for a standalone
  pack plus lifecycle-owned update flows.
- **Fold the dashboard into claudinite-tasks.** Removes the last cross-pack read, but the
  dashboard is a distinct capability a repo chooses separately. Rejected in favor of the
  `shared-code/` surface.
- **Wire vocabulary as duplicated data with drift guards.** Keeps packs fully
  import-independent, but the anchor math is logic rather than data, and every consumer copy is
  a drift liability. Rejected in favor of one published surface.
- **Delivery helpers as an engine residue.** Keeps `land-pr`/`deliver-generated` importable
  without a sanctioned crossing, but leaves task-lane capability in an engine meant to be
  distribution only. Rejected; they are `shared-code/`.
- **A second engine-owned scheduler kept for updates only.** Guarantees a delivery lane even
  when the tasks pack is broken, at the cost of two schedulers. Rejected: the canary rehearsal
  gates releases, and the recovery path is a human session — acceptable for an opt-in updater.

configuration — everything of this pack *outside* `shared-code/` stays off-limits to other
packs, and no other pack gains an equivalent surface by existing.

What it carries is what external consumers demonstrably need: the work-item/dispatch **title
grammar** (§3 — a work item is a GitHub issue and its title is its identity), the
**outcome/status decode** over item labels including every legacy spelling (§4), the **anchor
math** (`periodMs`, `mostRecentAnchor`, `nextAnchor`), the **delivery helpers**
(`deliverGenerated`, `landPr`) and **GitHub client/REST helpers** any pack's worker uses to land
output, and task-declaration validation, which other packs' tests exercise.

Consumers: `claudinite-dashboard` (renders the queue's state; stays its own pack and declares
`requires: ['claudinite-tasks']`), and any pack whose tasks deliver PRs or generated files.

### Updates live in claudinite-lifecycle

The versioned update flows (engine update, pack update, install) are the `update` task's own
machinery and live in `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/`. They still execute from the freshly fetched
canon tree, so the flow code a member runs is always current; the old `updates/*` module paths
remain as callable shims until no fielded vendored worker names them (the rule that already
governs `updates/*` exports).

A repo that declares `claudinite-lifecycle` but not `claudinite-tasks` has no queue, so its
update task never runs: **updates are opt-in via the tasks pack**. The recovery and manual lane
is a human session running the update or adopt-pack skills — a member with a state it likes
keeps it, like any package manager without forced auto-update.

### Workflows: written once, then static

The two member workflow files are static after adoption: secrets travel as one fixed
`CLAUDINITE_SECRETS: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}` line (§14.4), the per-repo cron minute and anchor
hours are written once at adoption, and `run:` lines name **mount pack paths**
(`.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/…`) behind which everything converges nightly — a
release never edits the YAML again.

Consequently **no update flow touches `.github/workflows/`**, and the `pending-workflows/`
withhold lane does not exist: a structural change to the YAML itself (permissions, an actions
version bump) is an explicit, human-merged fleet PR event, not a lane the machinery must carry.
Adoption of `claudinite-tasks` (the adopt-pack skill, or bootstrap when the pack is declared at
init) scaffolds the two files and the CCR routine endpoints; the routines' stored prompts point
at the pack's operational documents in the mount.

Members' `claudinite-ci.yml` is untouched by any of this: it is seeded once by bootstrap when no
existing workflow runs the world sweep, is member-owned from then on, and belongs to the checks
surface.

### Alternatives considered

- **Scheduler in the engine.** Scheduling was 52% of core; every consumer vendored machinery
  only scheduled repos use, engine releases implied workflow-path churn, and "core" stopped
  meaning distribution. Rejected — the size and the boundary rot are what this boundary fixes.
- **Fold the queue into claudinite-lifecycle.** Removes the updates↔queue seam entirely, but
  couples "being a member" with "running scheduled work" — a repo could not take the lifecycle
  without the queue, and the tasks surface stops being independent. Rejected for a standalone
  pack plus lifecycle-owned update flows.
- **Fold the dashboard into claudinite-tasks.** Removes the last cross-pack read, but the
  dashboard is a distinct capability a repo chooses separately. Rejected in favor of the
  `shared-code/` surface.
- **Wire vocabulary as duplicated data with drift guards.** Keeps packs fully
  import-independent, but the anchor math is logic rather than data, and every consumer copy is
  a drift liability. Rejected in favor of one published surface.
- **Delivery helpers as an engine residue.** Keeps `land-pr`/`deliver-generated` importable
  without a sanctioned crossing, but leaves task-lane capability in an engine meant to be
  distribution only. Rejected; they are `shared-code/`.
- **A second engine-owned scheduler kept for updates only.** Guarantees a delivery lane even
  when the tasks pack is broken, at the cost of two schedulers. Rejected: the canary rehearsal
  gates releases, and the recovery path is a human session — acceptable for an opt-in updater.

The gap looks one command wide, and improvising a merge to close it costs more than the unlanded change does. Where a shared delivery procedure exists (Claudinite's `engine/scheduler/deliver-pr.md`), the merges it licenses — like the direct merge on a base branch that requires nothing, where the arm is rejected "clean status" by design — are the sanctioned path, not a workaround; anything outside them stays unlanded. An open PR plus a plain statement of what could not be armed and why is a complete, honest result. Re-try the mechanism on each run rather than assuming either state is permanent, and drop the workaround the moment it succeeds.

input.command:
cat > packs/claudinite-tasks/README.md <<'EOF'
# claudinite-tasks — scheduled work

Everything whose subject is task work: the work-item queue, the executor, the task contract and
its signals, calendar/anchor math, run records, code-work, and the delivery lane a task's output
lands through. Declaring this pack is what gives a repo scheduled work; a repo that does not
declare it runs none, which is a supported state rather than a degraded one.

The mechanism itself — the state machine, the generator, the executor's protocol, urgency and
forcing, recovery — is [docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md](../../docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md), and
authoring a task is the `writing-tasks` skill's subject. This file is the pack's own map.

## Layout

| Path | What lives there |
|---|---|
| `queue/` | the work item and its vocabulary, the scheduler run, the executor and its continuation, the drain, leases, readiness, the janitor's rules, the schedule board, workflow-failure escalation |
| `queue/tasks/` | the built-in tasks (`implement-request`) |
| `signals/` | the signal collectors a precondition is handed |
| `stubs/` | the two workflow files an adopting repo receives |
| `shared-code/` | the published import surface — see below |
| `tasks/` | this pack's own scheduled tasks: `task-janitor` (the queue's sweeps) and `usage-fold` (it folds this mechanism's run records and outcome labels) |
| `worldRules/` | the task-declaration checks |
| `test/` | the unit suite, and `test/sim/` — the simulator and its scenario suite, the mechanism's executable spec |
| `executor.md`, `queue/instructions.md`, `deliver-pr.md` | operational documents a member's routines and workers read out of their own mount at runtime |

## `shared-code/` — the one sanctioned cross-pack import

Another pack's code may import `packs/claudinite-tasks/shared-code/*`, and nothing else of this
pack. The `pack-independence` barrier's allow list names that directory; no other pack gains an
equivalent surface by existing.

| Module | What it publishes | Who reads it |
|---|---|---|
| `work-items.mjs` | the title grammar that is a work item's identity, the outcome/status decode over its labels, lease state, the dispatch vocabulary, and what a scheduler run would instantiate | claudinite-dashboard, claudinite-fleet-sheepdog |
| `anchors.mjs` | period length, and the instant a task's window last opened at or opens next | claudinite-dashboard |
| `delivery.mjs` | `landPr`, `deliverGenerated` — how a task's output becomes a landed PR or a regenerated file | any pack whose tasks deliver |
| `github.mjs` | the GitHub client and REST helpers, and the tracker issue a worker records on | any pack whose tasks reach GitHub |
| `signals.mjs` | the signal shapes a precondition is handed | packs asserting what their own tasks will see |
| `task-contract.mjs` | task-declaration validation, and precondition evaluation as the executor does it | every pack with tasks, in its own tests |
| `usage-format.mjs` | the usage aggregate's codec | claudinite-fleet-sheepdog's fleet-wide aggregator |

A pack whose **non-task** code reads any of these declares `requires: ['claudinite-tasks']`. A
pack's `tasks/` folder needs no declaration: a mount without this pack carries no `tasks/` at all,
since a task folder is inert without the queue that runs it.

## Adoption

The two workflow files and the routine endpoints cannot converge into place — `.github/workflows/`
is the one directory a member's nightly update may never write — so they are scaffolded once, at
adoption, by the `adopt-pack` skill. They are static from then on: the per-repo cron minute and
anchor hours are written once, secrets travel as one fixed line, and the `run:` lines name mount
pack paths behind which everything converges nightly.

## The legacy `engine/scheduler/` shims

Until #1317's execution chain finishes, `engine/scheduler/*` still exists as one-line re-exports of
this pack, for members whose vendored workers, workflow `run:` lines and stored routine prompts
still name the old paths. They ship only into a mount that carries this pack, and they are deleted
once no fielded member names one.
EOF
git add packs/claudinite-tasks/README.md && echo ok

only to extend the *mechanism*, never to add one project's rule or task:

| Engine piece | Home | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| Checks runner + hooks | [`checks/`](engine/checks/README.md) | the dependency-free runner, its lib, the Stop hook, the PreToolUse guard — runs the packs' checks; owns no rule itself |
| Pack discovery + rules index | `engine/pack_loader/pack-registry.mjs`, `engine/pack_loader/generate-rules-index.mjs` | structural scan of `packs/*/pack.mjs`; the generated `@`-import index the repo's CLAUDE.md loads the active packs' prose through (#807) |
| Skill mounting | `engine/pack_loader/mount-skills.mjs` | per-session symlink of the active packs' bundled-skill union (`<pack>/skills/<name>/`) |
| Adoption interviews | `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/skills/adopt-claudinite/interview.mjs` | the gap computation (a pack's declared questions minus the entry's stored answers) and the SessionStart nudge; owns no question itself — bundled in the adoption skill, resolved fail-soft by the engine |
| Baseline-migration mechanism | [`engine/migrations/`](engine/migrations/README.md) | the read-side resolver and write-side rename for a relocation; a record lives under the flow that owns it (the engine's, or `packs/<pack>/migrations/`), records are kept forever, and vendoring's 7-day recency window decides what ships to consumers |
| The task scheduler | [`packs/claudinite-tasks/`](docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md) | in each repo's own workflow: the hourly scheduler run discovers its active packs' `tasks/<name>/task.mjs` and instantiates each one's work item at its anchor; the executor picks an item, collects that task's signals, runs its precondition and hands off. Pack-agnostic, owns no task, depends on no pack |
| The executor | [`packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/instructions.md`](packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/instructions.md) | the agent side of the queue — the whole stored prompt of a repo's executor routine points here; it validates one work item, runs its task's worker against its own repo, and delivers at the task's outcome ceiling |
| Bootstrap / update | [`bootstrap.md`](bootstrap.md), [`bootstrap.mjs`](bootstrap.mjs) | adoption — the doc's fast path, mechanized by the one-shot script — and the idempotent per-repo re-run |
| The update flows | [`updates/`](updates/README.md) | canon-internal, never vendored: one runner per flow that moves a repo from the versions it has installed to the ones this canon ships — today the engine's (docs/versioned-updates/DESIGN.md) |

**The test for "is this core?"** — would *every* pack's content stop working without it? The
scheduler, the runner, the migration mechanism, the executor loop all pass; a lint for one
technology, a nightly release task, a naming rule all fail. Two responsibilities are core *by
ownership* even though they run as pack tasks: **update** (the baseline pack's daily task) and the
**daily-run** itself are Claudinite's job, not a pack's — the pack is only the delivery slot.

## What a pack contributes

=== 110-130 ===
2. **A new technology's conventions** → a new technology pack, with a `detect` fingerprint so
   `--init` seeds it when the technology is present (declaring it stays the project's call).
3. **A new scheduled maintenance behavior** → a `tasks/<name>/` directory on the owning pack (a
   `task.mjs` declaration plus its worker). Every declaring repo's scheduler discovers it
   automatically — **no edit to the scheduler, and no cron of its own.** This is the load-bearing
   case: "add a nightly job" must never become "add a stage to `packs/claudinite-tasks/`" or "add a
   `schedule:` workflow."
4. **A new project-class playbook** → a project-class pack.
5. **Extending the engine itself** — a new signal the scheduler collects, a new discovery rule, a
   new migration capability, a change to the executor loop — *is* the rare core change. Do it
   deliberately, and expect it to serve every pack, not one.

If a proposed change is a new file under `packs/claudinite-tasks/`, `checks/` (beyond the runner/lib), or a
new branch in the scheduler *for one task's sake*, stop: it almost certainly belongs in a pack.

## Relocating into a pack: retire the old home

input.command:
git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Extract the task execution surface into a claudinite-tasks pack

`engine/scheduler/` was 52% of the engine, and the engine's test — would every
pack's content stop working without it? — no longer held for it: a repo that
declares no tasks pack runs no scheduled work, and that is a supported state.

The whole surface moves to `packs/claudinite-tasks/`: the queue, the executor,
the task contract and its signals, calendar/anchor math, run records, code-work,
the delivery lane, the two workflow stubs, the operational documents, and the
simulator with its scenario suite as the pack's own `test/sim/`. The queue's
meta-machinery relocates in beside it — `task-janitor` from basics, `usage-fold`
from claudinite-growth, and the `task-declaration-shape` / `task-code-work-env`
checks.

`shared-code/` is the pack's published import surface and the one sanctioned
cross-pack import in the corpus; the `pack-independence` barrier's allow list
names that directory and nothing else. A pack's `tasks/` folder rides the tasks
pack rather than the pack that owns the task, so a mount without the queue
carries no task folders and the vendor set stays import-closed on both sides.

`engine/scheduler/*` remains as one-line re-exports for members whose vendored
workers, workflow `run:` lines and stored routine prompts still name the old
paths; `legacy-entry.mjs` rewrites `process.argv[1]` so a command-line entry
reached through a shim still runs as the program. Until the record that seeds
the pack into every member's declaration has converged, the pack ships to every
mount whether or not it is declared — a member's live workflows name its modules
by literal path, and a mount that dropped them mid-migration could not be fixed.

Refs #1317
EOF

PRs A and B of #1317, landed together because neither is green alone.

**A** — create `packs/claudinite-tasks/`, move `engine/scheduler/*` in with a `shared-code/` published surface, leave re-export shims at every old path, move `engine-tests/scheduler/` and `docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/` into the pack's `test/`, adjust the vendor set, add the barriers config sanctioning `shared-code/*`.

**B** — relocate `task-janitor` (from basics), `usage-fold` (from claudinite-growth) and the `task-declaration-shape` / `task-code-work-env` checks into the pack, with `VERSIONS.md` rows in each source pack.

PR C (updates → claudinite-lifecycle, the converge-wiring split, bootstrap slimming, adopt-pack scaffolding, the withhold lane, the seeding migration record) and the gated tail PR D are separate.

End state and rationale: `docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` **§18** (folded into the mechanism's own design doc — no standalone document).

## Agreed end state (summary — DESIGN.md §18 is authoritative)

- `packs/claudinite-tasks/` owns the whole task surface: queue, executor, signals, task contract, calendar/anchor math, dispatch, run-records, code-work, delivery helpers (`land-pr`, `deliver-generated`), GitHub REST helpers, the two workflow stubs, the operational `.md`s, and the `implement-request` built-in as an ordinary pack task.
- `packs/claudinite-tasks/shared-code/*` is the pack's published import surface — the one sanctioned cross-pack import in the corpus (barriers-enforced). Consumers: claudinite-dashboard (title grammar, outcome decode, anchor math) and every pack task that delivers (delivery + gh helpers).
- Queue meta-machinery relocates in: `task-janitor` (from basics), `usage-fold` (from claudinite-growth), the task-declaration checks (from claudinite-growth worldRules) — and the simulator + scenario suite (`docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/`), the mechanism's executable spec, into the pack's own `test/`.
- The update flows (`updates/*`) move into `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/`; old `updates/*` paths stay as callable shims until no fielded vendored worker names them.
- `converge-wiring` splits: distribution wiring (hooks, rules index, gitattributes, badges) stays engine; workflow/scheduling wiring moves to the pack. Bootstrap stops wiring task machinery; adopting `claudinite-tasks` scaffolds it.
- The `pending-workflows/` withhold lane is deleted: after #1302 and #1290 the member workflow files are static (one-time cron at setup, `run:` lines pointing at stable mount pack paths). A structural YAML change is an explicit human-supported fleet PR event.
- A repo without `claudinite-tasks` runs no scheduled work and updates via a human session (update/adopt-pack skills) — no forced auto-update.
- Wire protocol (item titles, labels, run-record lines) is unchanged; legacy `engine/implement-request` titles decode forever.

## Plan

**Phase 0 — out-of-band setup:** none required. No new secret, permission, or platform setting; #1302 already removed the secrets variance.

**Review pass — one PR stack, approved together:**
- [ ] PR A — create `packs/claudinite-tasks/`: move `engine/scheduler/*` in (with `shared-code/`), leave re-export shims at every old `engine/scheduler/*` path a fielded caller names, adjust the vendor set (operational-`.md` whitelist paths, engine walk), move `engine-tests/scheduler/` **and `docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/` (sim.mjs, scenarios.test.mjs, coverage.test.mjs)** into the pack's `test/` (SCENARIOS.md stays in docs/ as the play-through record, its sim links repointed), add the barriers config sanctioning `shared-code/*`.
- [ ] PR B — relocate `task-janitor`, `usage-fold`, and the two task-declaration checks into the pack; `VERSIONS.md` rows in each source pack.
- [ ] PR C — `updates/*` → `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/` with old-path shims; split `converge-wiring`; slim bootstrap (no task wiring); `adopt-pack` scaffolding for claudinite-tasks (workflows, hashed cron, dailyHour, endpoints interview); delete the withhold lane; migration record seeding `claudinite-tasks` into member declarations.
- [ ] PR D (gated tail — written and approved now, merged by chain link L4): delete the old-path shims and any withhold leftovers.

**Execution chain** — each link filed as a sub-issue on approval of this plan, `Blocked-by:` the previous:
- [ ] L1 — force `fleet-baseline` with follow; exit: every member's stamp shows the pack version that ships claudinite-tasks, read from stamps, not run conclusions.
- [ ] L2 — manual fleet pass (owner-supported): repoint each member's two workflow files' `run:` lines and the CCR routine stored-prompt pointers (`executor.md`, `queue/instructions.md`) to the mount pack paths; exit: each member's next scheduler run green from the pack path.
- [ ] L3 — observe one full queue cycle fleet-wide (the update task converges through the pack executor); exit: every member's stamp moved after L2.
- [ ] L4 — merge PR D; exit: fleet self-tests green on the shim-free mount.

- `packs/claudinite-tasks/` owns the whole task surface: queue, executor, signals, task contract, calendar/anchor math, dispatch, run-records, code-work, delivery helpers (`land-pr`, `deliver-generated`), GitHub REST helpers, the two workflow stubs, the operational `.md`s, and the `implement-request` built-in as an ordinary pack task.
- `packs/claudinite-tasks/shared-code/*` is the pack's published import surface — the one sanctioned cross-pack import in the corpus (barriers-enforced). Consumers: claudinite-dashboard (title grammar, outcome decode, anchor math) and every pack task that delivers (delivery + gh helpers).
- Queue meta-machinery relocates in: `task-janitor` (from basics), `usage-fold` (from claudinite-growth), the task-declaration checks (from claudinite-growth worldRules) — and the simulator + scenario suite (`docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/`), the mechanism's executable spec, into the pack's own `test/`.

- The `pending-workflows/` withhold lane is deleted: after #1302 and #1290 the member workflow files are static (one-time cron at setup, `run:` lines pointing at stable mount pack paths). A structural YAML change is an explicit human-supported fleet PR event.
- A repo without `claudinite-tasks` runs no scheduled work and updates via a human session (update/adopt-pack skills) — no forced auto-update.

input.title: Extract the task execution surface into a claudinite-tasks pack
input.head: claude/pack-migration-tasks-9hw4tq
input.body:
PRs A and B of #1317, landed together because neither is green alone: the vendor set's import-closure guard is what forces the two halves into one change.

Closes #1325

## What moved

`engine/scheduler/*` → `packs/claudinite-tasks/` — the queue, the executor, the task contract and its signals, calendar/anchor math, run records, code-work, the delivery lane, the two workflow stubs and the three operational documents. `engine-tests/scheduler/` and `docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/` become the pack's own `test/` and `test/sim/`; `SCENARIOS.md` stays in `docs/` with its links repointed.

Relocated in beside it: `task-janitor` (from basics), `usage-fold` (from claudinite-growth), and the `task-declaration-shape` / `task-code-work-env` checks.

## `shared-code/` — the published surface

Eight modules, one per subject: `work-items`, `anchors`, `delivery`, `github`, `signals`, `task-contract`, `usage-format`, `wake`. The `pack-independence` barrier's allow list names that directory and nothing else. `claudinite-dashboard` declares `requires: ['claudinite-tasks']`; every other consumer reaches it only from a `tasks/` folder, and a pack's `tasks/` now rides the tasks pack rather than the pack that owns the task — so a mount without the queue carries no task folders and closure holds on both sides.

`wake.mjs` is its own module rather than a line in `work-items.mjs`: the dashboard loads that one unbundled in a browser, where the scheduler run's Node built-ins do not resolve.

## Compatibility

`engine/scheduler/*` remains as one-line re-exports for members whose vendored workers, workflow `run:` lines and stored routine prompts still name the old paths. `legacy-entry.mjs` rewrites `process.argv[1]` before the re-export evaluates, so a command-line entry reached through a shim still runs as the program rather than silently defining exports and exiting. The three operational `.md`s are replaced by "moved" pointers. The shims are a reviewed barrier exception and PR D deletes them.

**One migration tolerance to review**: until the record that seeds `claudinite-tasks` into every member's declaration lands (PR C), the pack ships to every mount whether or not it is declared. A member's live workflows name its modules by literal path, and a mount that dropped them mid-migration could not be fixed by any later converge. The removal condition is stated at the code: no member's stamp lacking the pack — not a date.

## Two behaviour changes worth a look

- `scheduler-workflow-shape` now accepts the pack entry path **and** the legacy engine one, so a member's un-convergeable workflow file is not a blocking finding during the window.
- `task-declaration-shape` skips a `task.mjs` that only re-exports another module: a relocation shim declares nothing of its own, and the real declaration is scanned where it lives. Tested by seeing it fail without the guard.

## Not in this PR

PR C (`updates/*` → claudinite-lifecycle, the `converge-wiring` split, bootstrap slimming, adopt-pack scaffolding, deleting the withhold lane, the seeding migration record) and the gated tail PR D. `implement-request` also stays a built-in under `queue/tasks/` for now rather than becoming an ordinary pack task.

## Verification

Full suite `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 2705 tests, 0 failures, with the clone deepened so `engine-pack-lane-shims` actually walks the trunk's pack history and confirms every fielded pack→engine import still resolves through a shim. `check_the_work` clean; `check_the_world` 0 blocking. The remaining advisories are `file-placement` on the shim files themselves — deliberate, and gone with PR D.

## Folders touched

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/   new pack: the moved surface, shared-code/, the two
                          relocated tasks, the two relocated checks, test/ and
                          test/sim/, pack.mjs / README / VERSIONS / badge
engine/scheduler/         now only re-export shims plus legacy-entry.mjs
engine/checks/, engine/hooks/
                          prose no longer names a pack by path (barrier)
vendoring/                the engine walk gates the shims on the pack; a pack's
                          tasks/ rides the tasks pack; the engine .md whitelist
                          is gone (a pack's .md is payload)
packs/basics, claudinite-growth, claudinite-dashboard,
```

PR A and PR B are up together in #1326 (sub-issue #1325). They could not land separately: the vendor set's import-closure guard fails the moment `claudinite-dashboard` and `claudinite-growth` name a pack that half the corpus still reaches through `engine/scheduler/`.

Three decisions this slice made that the plan left open, all reviewable in the PR:

1. **A pack's `tasks/` folder rides the tasks pack**, not the pack that owns the task. That is what keeps closure true for `basics`, `claudinite-lifecycle` and `claudinite-growth` without any of them declaring `requires: ['claudinite-tasks']` — which would have made the tasks pack universal and contradicted §18. Only `claudinite-dashboard`, whose non-task code reads the queue, declares the requires.

2. **A migration tolerance**: until PR C's seeding record has converged, `claudinite-tasks` ships to every mount whether declared or not. Without it, the first member to converge on this engine loses the modules its own workflows name by literal path, with nothing left able to fix it. The removal condition is at the code — no member's stamp lacking the pack, not a date.

3. **The shims need more than a re-export.** A command-line entry decides it is the program by comparing `import.meta.url` to `process.argv[1]`; reached through a shim, that comparison fails and `node .../engine/scheduler/queue/scheduler-run.mjs` would define exports and exit 0. `engine/scheduler/legacy-entry.mjs` rewrites the path first, and every shim imports it before its re-export.

Also deferred out of PR A: `implement-request` stays a built-in under `queue/tasks/` rather than becoming an ordinary pack task — that changes its wire id, so it belongs with the decode work, not the move.

14:import { NEEDS_HUMAN_LABEL } from '../../claudinite-tasks/dispatch.mjs';
# `updates/` — the flows that move a repo between versions

Canon-internal machinery (never vendored, like [`vendoring/`](../vendoring/README.md)): one runner
per **flow**, each moving a repo from the versions it has installed to the ones this canon tree
ships. The design — why the corpus splits into a versioned engine and versioned packs, and what
each flow may and may not do — is [`docs/versioned-updates/DESIGN.md`](../docs/versioned-updates/DESIGN.md);
the release discipline the engine's versions follow is [`engine/RELEASES.md`](../engine/RELEASES.md).

| File | Flow |
|---|---|
| [`engine-update.mjs`](engine-update.mjs) | The **engine update**: replace the mount's engine wholesale, run the engine migrations in the repo's gap, converge the non-workflow wiring, stamp the new version, and gate the merge on the converged tree's own `selftest --strict`. Deterministic end to end — no agentic stage, and no lane to add one. |
| [`pack-update.mjs`](pack-update.mjs) | The **pack update**: the same shape, per declared pack — replace the pack's tree, run its records, stamp its version, same gate. It enforces `minEngineVersion` against the version the TARGET runs, it may write `.github/workflows/` (which the engine flow may not), and it ends by saying whether the agentic apply stage is needed. |
| [`install.mjs`](install.mjs) | The **install**: the pack flow started from version zero, **running no migrations** — the vendored content is already the newest shape, and a record assumes the shapes its own era produced, which an empty repo is not. It stamps the latest version directly, and refuses a pack the repo already has a version for. |
| [`terminals.mjs`](terminals.mjs) | The **uniform terminal**: what happens to an update's PR, given what a flow returned. One function for every flow, so no shell re-decides it. |

The **skew guard** — which mechanism serves a repo while baselining and these flows
both exist — lives in [`engine/served-by.mjs`](../engine/served-by.mjs) rather than
here, because baselining's worker runs from a member's vendored mount and must read
the same definition these flows do.

Move the update flows into claudinite-lifecycle and split the wiring converge

PR C of #1317. Three changes that only make sense together, because each one is
what lets the next stop touching a member's workflow files.

The versioned update flows move to `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/`, beside
the task that owns them. A pack's `updates/` is canon-internal for the same
reason its `test/` is — the flows run from the canon tree the runner just
fetched, and reach canon-only machinery no mount carries — so the vendor set
excludes the directory by name. `updates/*` stays as re-export shims: a member's
update worker resolves those paths literally against that fetched tree and is
copied once, stale forever.

The wiring converge splits. `engine/converge-wiring.mjs` keeps distribution
wiring — hooks, the rules index and its CLAUDE.md import, the .gitattributes
entries, the badge row, the repo's own local pack — which every member carries.
The two workflow files become `packs/claudinite-tasks/converge-workflows.mjs`,
scaffolded once at adoption by bootstrap or the adopt-pack skill, because their
subject is the mechanism that runs them and a repo without it carries neither.

With that, no flow computes or writes a `.github/workflows/` path, so the
withhold staging lane is retired: nothing is staged, the emptied exports still
answer for a stale worker, and the flow sweeps whatever an earlier cycle left
under `.claudinite/pending-workflows/`.

A migration record declares `claudinite-tasks` into every member that carries a
scheduler workflow — the one artifact that says what a repo actually does rather
than what its declaration hoped. That record converging fleet-wide is the
condition on the vendor set's temporary tolerance, read off stamps, not a date.

Refs #1317
EOF

input.title: Extract the task surface into claudinite-tasks, move the update flows, split the wiring converge
input.body:
PRs A, B and C of #1317. Landed together because none of them is green alone: the vendor set's import-closure guard forces A and B into one change, and until C stops every flow from touching `.github/workflows/`, the wiring converge still needs a stub the engine no longer owns.

Closes #1325

## A — the surface moves

`engine/scheduler/*` → `packs/claudinite-tasks/` — the queue, the executor, the task contract and its signals, calendar/anchor math, run records, code-work, the delivery lane, the two workflow stubs and the three operational documents. `engine-tests/scheduler/` and `docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/` become the pack's own `test/` and `test/sim/`; `SCENARIOS.md` stays in `docs/` with its links repointed.

## B — the queue's meta-machinery follows it

`task-janitor` (from basics), `usage-fold` (from claudinite-growth), and the `task-declaration-shape` / `task-code-work-env` checks.

## C — updates move, and the wiring converge splits

The versioned update flows move to `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/`. A pack's `updates/` is canon-internal for the same reason its `test/` is — the flows run from the canon tree the runner just fetched and reach canon-only machinery no mount carries — so the vendor set excludes the directory by name.

`engine/converge-wiring.mjs` keeps distribution wiring (hooks, rules index and its CLAUDE.md import, `.gitattributes`, badge row, the repo's own local pack). The two workflow files become `packs/claudinite-tasks/converge-workflows.mjs`, scaffolded once at adoption by bootstrap or the adopt-pack skill.

With that, **no flow computes or writes a `.github/workflows/` path**, so the withhold staging lane is retired: nothing is staged, the emptied exports still answer for a stale worker, and the flow sweeps whatever an earlier cycle left under `.claudinite/pending-workflows/`.

A migration record declares `claudinite-tasks` into every member that carries a scheduler workflow — the one artifact that says what a repo actually does rather than what its declaration hoped.

## `shared-code/` — the one sanctioned cross-pack import

Eight modules: `work-items`, `anchors`, `delivery`, `github`, `signals`, `task-contract`, `usage-format`, `wake`. The `pack-independence` barrier's allow list names that directory and nothing else. `claudinite-dashboard` declares `requires: ['claudinite-tasks']`; every other consumer reaches it only from a `tasks/` folder, and a pack's `tasks/` now rides the tasks pack — so a mount without the queue carries no task folders and closure holds on both sides.

`wake.mjs` is its own module rather than a line in `work-items.mjs`: the dashboard loads that one unbundled in a browser, where the scheduler run's Node built-ins do not resolve.

## Compatibility

`engine/scheduler/*` and `updates/*` remain as one-line re-exports for members whose vendored workers, workflow `run:` lines and stored routine prompts still name the old paths. Each tree has a `legacy-entry.mjs` that rewrites `process.argv[1]` before the re-export evaluates, so a command-line entry reached through a shim still runs as the program rather than silently defining exports and exiting. `engine/scheduler/converge-wiring.mjs` additionally keeps the old four-argument signature and its own CLI, since the split changed both. All of it is a reviewed barrier exception, and PR D deletes it.

**One migration tolerance to review**: until the seeding record has converged fleet-wide, the vendor set ships `claudinite-tasks` whether or not a member declares it. A member's live workflows name its modules by literal path, and a mount that dropped them mid-migration could not be fixed by any later converge. The removal condition is stated at the code — no member's stamp lacking the pack, not a date.

## Three behaviour changes worth a look

- `scheduler-workflow-shape` accepts the pack entry path **and** the legacy engine one, so a member's un-convergeable workflow file is not a blocking finding during the window.
- `task-declaration-shape` skips a `task.mjs` that only re-exports another module: a relocation shim declares nothing of its own. Tested by seeing it fail without the guard.
- The `claudinite-canary-repo` pack exists to rehearse the withhold lane, which this PR retires. Its manifest now says so; **what to do with the pack is left open** rather than decided here.

## Not in this PR

PR D, the gated tail that deletes the shims once L1–L3 confirm no member names one. `implement-request` also stays a built-in under `queue/tasks/` rather than becoming an ordinary pack task — that changes its wire id, so it belongs with the decode work.

## Verification

Full suite `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 0 failures, with the clone deepened so `engine-pack-lane-shims` actually walks the trunk's pack history and confirms every fielded pack→engine import still resolves through a shim. `check_the_work` clean; `check_the_world` 0 blocking. The remaining advisories are `file-placement` on the shim files themselves — deliberate, and gone with PR D.

## Folders touched

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/       new pack: the moved surface, shared-code/, the two
                              relocated tasks, the two relocated checks, the
                              workflow scaffolder, the seeding migration record,
                              test/ and test/sim/
packs/claudinite-lifecycle/   updates/ moves in (canon-internal); the update
                              task's staged-delivery step becomes a sweep;
                              scheduler-workflow-shape accepts both entry paths
engine/                       converge-wiring.mjs is the distribution half;
                              engine/scheduler/ is now only re-export shims plus
                              legacy-entry.mjs; prose no longer names a pack
updates/                      re-export shims plus legacy-entry.mjs
vendoring/                    the engine walk gates the shims on the pack; a
                              pack's tasks/ rides the tasks pack; a pack's
                              updates/ never vendors; the engine .md whitelist is
                              gone (a pack's .md is payload)
bootstrap.mjs                 distribution wiring always; workflow scaffolding
                              only when the tasks pack is in the mount
packs/basics, claudinite-growth, claudinite-dashboard, claudinite-fleet-sheepdog,
packs/chrome-extension, product-wiki, tidy-repo, claudinite-canary-repo
                              imports repointed at shared-code/, versions bumped
.github/workflows/            the canon's own run: lines and the ci.yml test roots
.claudinite-settings.json     the pack declaration, the barrier exceptions and
                              the canon-internal updates/ carve-out
.claudinite/local/packs/      the thin-workflow rule, promote-scope fixtures, and
                              the pack-independence allow list
docs/                         §18 records the shipped shared-code surface and the
                              updates move; versioned-updates §  marks the
                              withhold lane superseded
```

input.body:
PRs A, B and C of #1317, landed together in #1326 because none is green alone.

**A** — create `packs/claudinite-tasks/`, move `engine/scheduler/*` in with a `shared-code/` published surface, leave re-export shims at every old path, move `engine-tests/scheduler/` and `docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/` into the pack's `test/`, adjust the vendor set, add the barriers config sanctioning `shared-code/*`.

**B** — relocate `task-janitor` (from basics), `usage-fold` (from claudinite-growth) and the `task-declaration-shape` / `task-code-work-env` checks into the pack, with `VERSIONS.md` rows in each source pack.

**C** — `updates/*` → `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/` with old-path shims; split `converge-wiring` (distribution stays engine, the two workflow files become the pack's `converge-workflows.mjs`); slim bootstrap; adopt-pack scaffolding; delete the withhold lane; the migration record seeding `claudinite-tasks` into member declarations.

The gated tail PR D — deleting the shims — is separate, merged by chain link L4.

input.body:
Comment class: other

PR C is on the same branch, so #1326 now carries A, B and C. Suite green, `check_the_work` clean, `check_the_world` 0 blocking.

What C settled, beyond the plan's wording:

1. **A pack's `updates/` is canon-internal, by directory name.** Moving the flows under `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/` would otherwise vendor them into every member — and they import `vendoring/compute-vendor-set.mjs`, which no mount carries, so the coherence guard would abort every converge. The exclusion is the same rule shape as `test/`, and it is also what makes the flows' `docs/` and `vendoring/` references legitimate: both barriers now carve that directory out, with the reason on the rule.

2. **The wiring converge splits by who owns the file, not by who can push it.** `engine/converge-wiring.mjs` is distribution; `packs/claudinite-tasks/converge-workflows.mjs` is the two workflow files, scaffolded at adoption only. Retiring the withhold lane falls out of that rather than being a separate decision: once no flow computes a workflow, there is nothing to stage.

3. **The seeding record gates on the member's own scheduler workflow**, not on a declaration or a stamp. A repo without that file chose no queue, and seeding the pack there would hand it tasks nobody asked for.

Two things I did not decide:

- **PR D** needs its own branch, and my dispatch designates only this one. Say the word and I'll write it.
- **`claudinite-canary-repo`** existed to rehearse the withhold lane. Its manifest now states the lane is retired and its probe exercises a route that no longer exists; nothing depends on it, and I left the pack in place rather than delete it inside this change.

Seed claudinite-tasks at --init, and gate bootstrap's scaffold on the declaration

Two defects the no-tasks-pack path exposed, both mine from the wiring split.

Bootstrap gated the workflow scaffold on the module being present in the mount,
but the migration tolerance ships that module to every mount — so a repo that
declared no tasks pack got a queue it never asked for. The gate is the
declaration, which is what decides activation everywhere else.

makes the directory it needs.

A new repo still gets scheduled work: `claudinite-tasks` is seeded by `--init`
like tidy-repo, so the opt-out is removing the declaration rather than never
receiving it — a member with no queue never runs the update task that keeps its
Claudinite current.

Refs #1317
EOF

input.title: Delete the legacy shims left by the claudinite-tasks extraction
input.head: claude/pack-migration-tasks-shim-removal
input.body:
PR D of #1317 — the gated tail. Written now so the stack takes one approval, **merged only at chain link L4**.

Closes #1328

> ⚠️ **Do not merge yet.** L1 must show every member's stamp carrying the pack, L2 must repoint each member's workflow `run:` lines and routine prompts, and L3 must observe a full queue cycle running from the new paths. Merging before that leaves members whose live workflows name files this PR deletes, with nothing able to repair them.

Based on `claude/pack-migration-tasks-9hw4tq` (#1326), so the diff shows only the deletion.

## What goes

- `engine/scheduler/*` and `updates/*` — both shim trees, each with its `legacy-entry.mjs`.
- The reviewed barrier exception that let `engine/scheduler/` name a pack.
- The vendor set's two temporary rules: the engine walk that shipped the shims only where the pack shipped, and the tolerance that shipped `claudinite-tasks` whether or not a member declared it. Past L3 the declaration decides, with nothing added to it.

## Two tests carry the confirmation

The point of the chain is that the retirement is *observed*, not assumed, so the tests say which:

- `engine-pack-lane-shims` gains a `RETIRED` list holding `engine/scheduler/*`. The condition for putting a path there is written at the definition: its fielded callers were read and found gone — never "the current tree does not import it", which is the one thing the scan exists because you cannot rely on.
- The fielded-flow surface in `install.test.mjs` names the flows at `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/`, which is the same fact from the other side: a worker one cycle behind loads them from the canon tree it just fetched.

Two canon call sites that had been going through the `updates/` shim now name the real path; one dangling link in the canary pack's README is repointed.

## Verification

Full suite 0 failures; `check_the_work` clean; `check_the_world` 0 blocking. The advisory count drops from 142 to 84 — the difference is the `file-placement` advisories the shim files were carrying.

## Folders touched

```
engine/scheduler/         deleted
updates/                  deleted
vendoring/                the shim gating and the undeclared-pack tolerance come out
.claudinite-settings.json the engine/scheduler barrier exception comes out
```

input.title: claudinite-tasks L1: force fleet-baseline, and read the pack version off every stamp
input.body:
Chain link L1 of #1317, once #1326 has merged.

Drive Shepherd's `fleet-baseline` with `follow`, and report per member unasked.

**Exit condition:** every member's stamp carries a `claudinite-tasks` version — read from the stamps themselves, never from run conclusions, which say only that a job finished.

Two things this pass also confirms, because they are what the rest of the chain is gated on: that the seeding migration record reached each member that carries a scheduler workflow, and that no member's mount lost `engine/scheduler/` while its workflows still name it (the vendor set's tolerance is what prevents that, and this is where it either holds or does not).

Blocked-by: #1325

input.title: claudinite-tasks L2: repoint every member's workflow run: lines and routine prompts
input.body:
Chain link L2 of #1317. Owner-supported: `.github/workflows/` is the one directory a converge cannot push to, and the CCR routine prompts are a console setting.

Per member, two edits:

- **The two workflow files.** Each `run:` line moves from `.claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/…` to `.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/…`. The pack ships `converge-workflows.mjs`, which writes exactly what a member should be carrying — running it in the member is the mechanical way to produce the diff rather than hand-editing five lines.
- **The two routine stored prompts.** The executor's points at `executor.md`, the work-item session's at `queue/instructions.md`, both under the pack's mount path now. Until this lands, each still resolves through a pointer file that says "moved" and names the new path — a session can follow it, but it costs a hop and the pointer goes away at L4.

**Exit condition:** each member's next scheduler run is green, running from the pack path.

Blocked-by: #1330

input.title: claudinite-tasks L3: observe one full queue cycle fleet-wide from the pack paths
input.body:
Chain link L3 of #1317.

Watch one complete cycle on every member: the scheduler run files its items, the drain dispatches the executor, and the update task converges through the pack's executor rather than the engine's old entry point.

**Exit condition:** every member's stamp has moved *after* L2 landed. A stamp that has not moved is a member whose queue is not actually running from the new paths, whatever its workflow file says — and it is the one signal that separates "the repoint was merged" from "the repoint works".

This is also what licenses two things #1326 left deliberately temporary: the vendor set's tolerance that ships `claudinite-tasks` to undeclared members, and the shims PR D deletes. Both come out on the strength of this observation, not a date.

Blocked-by: #1331

## Agreed end state (summary — DESIGN.md §18 is authoritative)

- `packs/claudinite-tasks/` owns the whole task surface: queue, executor, signals, task contract, calendar/anchor math, dispatch, run-records, code-work, delivery helpers (`land-pr`, `deliver-generated`), GitHub REST helpers, the two workflow stubs, the operational `.md`s, and the `implement-request` built-in as an ordinary pack task.
- `packs/claudinite-tasks/shared-code/*` is the pack's published import surface — the one sanctioned cross-pack import in the corpus (barriers-enforced). Consumers: claudinite-dashboard (title grammar, outcome decode, anchor math) and every pack task that delivers (delivery + gh helpers).
- Queue meta-machinery relocates in: `task-janitor` (from basics), `usage-fold` (from claudinite-growth), the task-declaration checks (from claudinite-growth worldRules) — and the simulator + scenario suite (`docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/`), the mechanism's executable spec, into the pack's own `test/`.

- The `pending-workflows/` withhold lane is deleted: after #1302 and #1290 the member workflow files are static (one-time cron at setup, `run:` lines pointing at stable mount pack paths). A structural YAML change is an explicit human-supported fleet PR event.

- Wire protocol (item titles, labels, run-record lines) is unchanged; legacy `engine/implement-request` titles decode forever.

End state and rationale: `docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` **§18** (folded into the mechanism's own design doc — no standalone document).

## Agreed end state (summary — DESIGN.md §18 is authoritative)

- `packs/claudinite-tasks/` owns the whole task surface: queue, executor, signals, task contract, calendar/anchor math, dispatch, run-records, code-work, delivery helpers (`land-pr`, `deliver-generated`), GitHub REST helpers, the two workflow stubs, the operational `.md`s, and the `implement-request` built-in as an ordinary pack task.
- `packs/claudinite-tasks/shared-code/*` is the pack's published import surface — the one sanctioned cross-pack import in the corpus (barriers-enforced). Consumers: claudinite-dashboard (title grammar, outcome decode, anchor math) and every pack task that delivers (delivery + gh helpers).
- Queue meta-machinery relocates in: `task-janitor` (from basics), `usage-fold` (from claudinite-growth), the task-declaration checks (from claudinite-growth worldRules) — and the simulator + scenario suite (`docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/`), the mechanism's executable spec, into the pack's own `test/`.
- The update flows (`updates/*`) move into `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/`; old `updates/*` paths stay as callable shims until no fielded vendored worker names them.
- `converge-wiring` splits: distribution wiring (hooks, rules index, gitattributes, badges) stays engine; workflow/scheduling wiring moves to the pack. Bootstrap stops wiring task machinery; adopting `claudinite-tasks` scaffolds it.
- The `pending-workflows/` withhold lane is deleted: after #1302 and #1290 the member workflow files are static (one-time cron at setup, `run:` lines pointing at stable mount pack paths). A structural YAML change is an explicit human-supported fleet PR event.
- A repo without `claudinite-tasks` runs no scheduled work and updates via a human session (update/adopt-pack skills) — no forced auto-update.
- Wire protocol (item titles, labels, run-record lines) is unchanged; legacy `engine/implement-request` titles decode forever.

## Plan

**Phase 0 — out-of-band setup:** none required. No new secret, permission, or platform setting; #1302 already removed the secrets variance.

**Review pass — one PR stack, approved together:**
- [ ] PR A — create `packs/claudinite-tasks/`: move `engine/scheduler/*` in (with `shared-code/`), leave re-export shims at every old `engine/scheduler/*` path a fielded caller names, adjust the vendor set (operational-`.md` whitelist paths, engine walk), move `engine-tests/scheduler/` **and `docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/` (sim.mjs, scenarios.test.mjs, coverage.test.mjs)** into the pack's `test/` (SCENARIOS.md stays in docs/ as the play-through record, its sim links repointed), add the barriers config sanctioning `shared-code/*`.
- [ ] PR B — relocate `task-janitor`, `usage-fold`, and the two task-declaration checks into the pack; `VERSIONS.md` rows in each source pack.
- [ ] PR C — `updates/*` → `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/` with old-path shims; split `converge-wiring`; slim bootstrap (no task wiring); `adopt-pack` scaffolding for claudinite-tasks (workflows, hashed cron, dailyHour, endpoints interview); delete the withhold lane; migration record seeding `claudinite-tasks` into member declarations.
- [ ] PR D (gated tail — written and approved now, merged by chain link L4): delete the old-path shims and any withhold leftovers.

**Execution chain** — each link filed as a sub-issue on approval of this plan, `Blocked-by:` the previous:
- [ ] L1 — force `fleet-baseline` with follow; exit: every member's stamp shows the pack version that ships claudinite-tasks, read from stamps, not run conclusions.
- [ ] L2 — manual fleet pass (owner-supported): repoint each member's two workflow files' `run:` lines and the CCR routine stored-prompt pointers (`executor.md`, `queue/instructions.md`) to the mount pack paths; exit: each member's next scheduler run green from the pack path.
- [ ] L3 — observe one full queue cycle fleet-wide (the update task converges through the pack executor); exit: every member's stamp moved after L2.
- [ ] L4 — merge PR D; exit: fleet self-tests green on the shim-free mount.
