{"id":5232886655,"number":1317,"state":"open","locked":false,"title":"Extract the task execution/scheduling surface into a claudinite-tasks pack","body":"Tracking issue for the split of `engine/scheduler/` (52% of core, 8,106 lines) out of the engine and into a canon pack, so the engine is pack distribution only. End state and rationale: `docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` **§18** (folded into the mechanism's own design doc — no standalone document).

## Agreed end state (summary — DESIGN.md §18 is authoritative)

- `packs/claudinite-tasks/` owns the whole task surface: queue, executor, signals, task contract, calendar/anchor math, dispatch, run-records, code-work, delivery helpers (`land-pr`, `deliver-generated`), GitHub REST helpers, the two workflow stubs, the operational `.md`s, and the `implement-request` built-in as an ordinary pack task.
- `packs/claudinite-tasks/shared-code/*` is the pack's published import surface — the one sanctioned cross-pack import in the corpus (barriers-enforced). Consumers: claudinite-dashboard (title grammar, outcome decode, anchor math) and every pack task that delivers (delivery + gh helpers).
- Queue meta-machinery relocates in: `task-janitor` (from basics), `usage-fold` (from claudinite-growth), the task-declaration checks (from claudinite-growth worldRules) — and the simulator + scenario suite (`docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/`), the mechanism's executable spec, into the pack's own `test/`.
- The update flows (`updates/*`) move into `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/`; old `updates/*` paths stay as callable shims until no fielded vendored worker names them.
- `converge-wiring` splits: distribution wiring (hooks, rules index, gitattributes, badges) stays engine; workflow/scheduling wiring moves to the pack. Bootstrap stops wiring task machinery; adopting `claudinite-tasks` scaffolds it.
- The `pending-workflows/` withhold lane is deleted: after #1302 and #1290 the member workflow files are static (one-time cron at setup, `run:` lines pointing at stable mount pack paths). A structural YAML change is an explicit human-supported fleet PR event.
- A repo without `claudinite-tasks` runs no scheduled work and updates via a human session (update/adopt-pack skills) — no forced auto-update.
- Wire protocol (item titles, labels, run-record lines) is unchanged; legacy `engine/implement-request` titles decode forever.

## Plan

**Phase 0 — out-of-band setup:** none required. No new secret, permission, or platform setting; #1302 already removed the secrets variance.

**Review pass — one PR stack, approved together:**
- [ ] PR A — create `packs/claudinite-tasks/`: move `engine/scheduler/*` in (with `shared-code/`), leave re-export shims at every old `engine/scheduler/*` path a fielded caller names, adjust the vendor set (operational-`.md` whitelist paths, engine walk), move `engine-tests/scheduler/` **and `docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/` (sim.mjs, scenarios.test.mjs, coverage.test.mjs)** into the pack's `test/` (SCENARIOS.md stays in docs/ as the play-through record, its sim links repointed), add the barriers config sanctioning `shared-code/*`.
- [ ] PR B — relocate `task-janitor`, `usage-fold`, and the two task-declaration checks into the pack; `VERSIONS.md` rows in each source pack.
- [ ] PR C — `updates/*` → `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/` with old-path shims; split `converge-wiring`; slim bootstrap (no task wiring); `adopt-pack` scaffolding for claudinite-tasks (workflows, hashed cron, dailyHour, endpoints interview); delete the withhold lane; migration record seeding `claudinite-tasks` into member declarations.
- [ ] PR D (gated tail — written and approved now, merged by chain link L4): delete the old-path shims and any withhold leftovers.

**Execution chain** — each link filed as a sub-issue on approval of this plan, `Blocked-by:` the previous:
- [ ] L1 — force `fleet-baseline` with follow; exit: every member's stamp shows the pack version that ships claudinite-tasks, read from stamps, not run conclusions.
- [ ] L2 — manual fleet pass (owner-supported): repoint each member's two workflow files' `run:` lines and the CCR routine stored-prompt pointers (`executor.md`, `queue/instructions.md`) to the mount pack paths; exit: each member's next scheduler run green from the pack path.
- [ ] L3 — observe one full queue cycle fleet-wide (the update task converges through the pack executor); exit: every member's stamp moved after L2.
- [ ] L4 — merge PR D; exit: fleet self-tests green on the shim-free mount.

input.title: claudinite-canary-repo: the withhold lane it probes no longer exists
input.body:
The `claudinite-canary-repo` pack exists to rehearse one thing: the **withhold lane** — a `.github/workflows/` write diverted to `.claudinite/pending-workflows/`, carried in a maintenance PR, and moved into place by a session holding a credential the Action token does not have. Its probe workflow, its migration record's revision marker, and its README are all about that route.

#1317 retires the lane. A member's workflow files are static after adoption, so no flow computes or stages one, and nothing delivers a staged file any more. The pack's manifest now says so, but the probe still runs and still bumps a revision nobody reads a conclusion from.

Nothing depends on it, so nothing is urgent. Three shapes it could take:

- **Repurpose the probe.** Have it verify what still matters — that a member's scaffolded workflow files match the stubs `claudinite-tasks` ships, which is now the thing that can silently drift, since a converge cannot correct them.
- **Retire the pack.** Delete it, its record and its stub, and drop it from the catalog. Its premise is gone and a pack that reads as live but proves nothing is worse than none.
- **Leave it.** Cheapest, and wrong in the way the corpus keeps warning about: a mechanism that measures nothing looks identical to one that measures something.

Not decided in #1326 — widening that PR to delete a pack was the wrong place for the call.

Comment class: other — a command to execute the plan in [#1317](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1317).

The whole review pass is up.

**[#1326](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1326)** — PRs A + B + C, four commits on `claude/pack-migration-tasks-9hw4tq`. `engine/scheduler/` (8,796 lines) becomes `packs/claudinite-tasks/`; `task-janitor`, `usage-fold` and the two task-declaration checks move in beside it; the update flows move to `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/`; the wiring converge splits and the withhold lane is retired. Closes [#1325](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1325).

**[#1329](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1329)** — PR D, the gated tail, based on that branch so its diff is only the deletion. Closes [#1328](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1328). **Must not merge until L4.**

**Chain filed as sub-issues**, each blocked by the last: [#1330](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1330) (L1 force fleet-baseline, read the stamps) → [#1331](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1331) (L2 repoint workflows and routine prompts) → [#1332](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1332) (L3 observe a full cycle) → [#1328](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1328) (L4 merge PR D). Plus [#1333](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1333) for the canary pack, whose premise this change removes.

Three decisions the plan left open, all reviewable in the diffs:

- **A pack's `tasks/` rides the tasks pack, and its `updates/` never vendors.** Both fall out of the import-closure guard: without the first, `basics` and `claudinite-lifecycle` would have to `requires` the tasks pack, making it universal; without the second, the flows' `vendoring/` import lands in every member's tree.
- **One migration tolerance** ships `claudinite-tasks` to undeclared members until the seeding record converges. A member's live workflows name its modules by literal path, and a mount that dropped them mid-migration could not be repaired. Removal is gated on stamps, not a date — and PR D is where it comes out.
- **The shims need more than a re-export.** A command-line entry compares `import.meta.url` to `process.argv[1]`; reached through a shim that check fails, so `node …/queue/scheduler-run.mjs` would define exports and exit 0. Each shim tree has a `legacy-entry.mjs` that rewrites the path first.

Verification on both branches: full suite 0 failures (clone deepened so `engine-pack-lane-shims` actually walks the trunk's pack history), `check_the_work` clean, `check_the_world` 0 blocking.

> ⚠️ Still open: [#1326](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1326) and [#1329](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1329) await your review — and L1–L3 ([#1330](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1330), [#1331](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1331), [#1332](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1332)) are fleet-wide work I did not start.

content.text:
**Do the three decisions need you?** No — but a fourth one does, and I should have flagged it.

The three I listed are forced, not chosen. `tasks/` riding the tasks pack and `updates/` never vendoring are both the only shapes the vendor set's import-closure guard permits; the alternative to the first is making `basics` require the tasks pack, which would make it universal and contradict §18. The migration tolerance is a safety requirement with a stated removal condition. `legacy-entry.mjs` is mechanism.

The one that is genuinely yours: I set **`seededByDefault: true`** on `claudinite-tasks`, so `--init` seeds it into every new repo and the opt-out is removing the declaration. §18 describes the pack as opt-in, which would have meant new repos get no scheduler unless someone asks. I chose seeded because a member without a queue never runs the update task that keeps its Claudinite current. That's a policy call, it's reversible with a one-line change, and it's in [d346e61](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1326/commits)'s parent.

**Am I confident we can start the rollout?** I wasn't entitled to be an hour ago, and checking is what changed the answer. Your question sent me looking, and it found two real defects:

- `implement-request`'s worker path is *derived* from where its module sits, so the move silently changed what a new dispatch carries. `BUILT_IN_PATH_RE` is a validator, so it would have **rejected every new ad-hoc request** as a malformed task path — loudly, fleet-wide, on every request.
- `taskIdFromPath` is a fallback, so the same gap failed *silently*: a marked issue carries no id in its title, so every new request item would have been unattributable to the janitor, uncounted by usage-fold and blank on the dashboard.

Both are fixed and pinned by tests that also assert the path the code actually mints. Suite green on both branches, `check_the_world` 0 blocking, and CI on [#1326](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1326) is green.

So: **yes for L1**, which is a converge and a stamp read — the rehearsal covers exactly that shape and it passes on every fixture. **Not yet for L2**, and not because of a known problem: the class of bug I just found is "a path derived rather than written", and the only derivation left is `repoRootFrom`, which its test now exercises through a real vendored copy. But a canary member converging and draining one item would prove in an hour what I can only argue from fixtures. I'd run L1 against the canary alone first, watch one queue cycle there, and treat that as the gate on the fleet-wide pass.

> ⚠️ Still open: [#1326](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1326) needs review; the `seededByDefault` call is yours to confirm or reverse; and I'd gate L2 ([#1331](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1331)) on one canary member completing a queue cycle rather than going straight to the fleet.

content.content:
---
name: merge-to-main
description: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
---

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`), body ending `Closes #<issue>`.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it again.
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.
